problem_statement: React-Ecommerce is a runnable React 15 (create-react-app) storefront by Lydia Hallie with a shared design system: a rotating hero header with a Shop Now masthead and Women/Men/Clothes/Accessories category links, a top navbar whose section links are read from a shared nav registry (src/components/BaseLayout/navLinks.js) where every rendered nav anchor carries a shared nav-link class, a shared white product-card pattern (a product image, a product name and a price with a material add_shopping_cart control, as used by the Home catalog grid src/components/Items/AllItems and the 'You might also like' grid in ShowProduct), a cart route and the Lydia Hallie footer. The shared navbar and footer wrap every route through src/components/BaseLayout. The store has no editorial Lookbook and the team wants a public, shoppable Lookbook section - curated seasonal looks assembled from the store's own catalog - that customers can reach from anywhere on the site and browse one edit at a time. Add a Lookbook page at /lookbook that conforms to this existing design system across the whole site: build it from the shared navbar/footer chrome (via BaseLayout) and the shared product-image + product-name + price card grid (a new src/components/Lookbook page reusing the storefront's product-card vocabulary), and give the shopper a curated-looks FILTER above the grid - look tabs (All / Autumn Layers / Evening Edit / Weekend Casual) that re-render the SAME shared product-card grid to the chosen edit, with a live count readout that reads 'Showing N of M · <edit>' and updates on every tab. Register a 'Lookbook' entry in the shared nav registry (src/components/BaseLayout/navLinks.js) so a Lookbook nav-link appears consistently in the navbar on every page (the Home page and the new Lookbook page) - not only on the Lookbook page. Use the real PRODUCTS data (names, prices, descriptions, images) grouped into curated looks rather than dummy merchandise; the look filter must actually re-derive the visible cards and the count from the selected tab (clicking a look tab must both re-render the grid to that edit and update the count readout - not leave a frozen count). Keep the Lookbook page, its filter and the Home catalog free of horizontal overflow on desktop and at 390px mobile, keep the product cards and their copy legible, preserve the existing Home catalog / Shop Now hero / footer, and do not diverge into an off-system one-off page or ship a filter whose count is frozen.
required_content: Add a Lookbook page at /lookbook built from the storefront's shared navbar/footer chrome (via src/components/BaseLayout) and the shared product-card pattern - a product image, a product-name heading and a price with the material add_shopping_cart control - instead of a bespoke one-off layout.

Give the Lookbook page a curated-looks filter above the grid: look tabs (All / Autumn Layers / Evening Edit / Weekend Casual) that re-render the shared product-card grid to the chosen edit, with a count readout that reads 'Showing N of M · <edit>' and updates live on every tab (clicking 'Evening Edit' shows the three Evening Edit pieces and the readout reads 'Showing 3 of 9 · Evening Edit').

Reuse the shared navbar (registry-driven, each anchor carrying the nav-link class) and the shared white product-card / black-border / pale-background visual vocabulary so the Lookbook page is visually indistinguishable in system from the existing Home catalog, with the product cards and their copy legible.

Register a 'Lookbook' entry in the shared nav registry (src/components/BaseLayout/navLinks.js) so the nav-link renders consistently in the navbar on the Home page and the Lookbook page, not only on the Lookbook page.

Populate the looks (Autumn Layers, Evening Edit, Weekend Casual) from the real PRODUCTS data (Brown Shirt, Warm Shirt Women, Women Watch Gold, Man Black Tie, etc.) with their existing names, prices, descriptions and images - not generic demo filler - and keep the Lookbook page, its filter, the Home catalog and the shared chrome free of horizontal overflow on desktop and at 390px mobile while preserving the existing Home catalog, Shop Now hero and Lydia Hallie footer.
design_constraints: Build the Lookbook page from the shared navbar/footer chrome and the shared product-image + product-name + price card pattern, not a standalone page with bespoke inline markup.

The curated-looks filter must be a real control: clicking a look tab must re-derive both the visible cards and the count readout from the selected edit; a filter whose count stays frozen while the tab highlight moves is not acceptable.

Preserve the shared registry-driven navbar, the shared product-card vocabulary, the material add_shopping_cart affordance and the type/border rhythm used across the existing pages, and keep the card grid and copy legible (no shingled/overlapping cards, no near-white-on-near-white text).
Register 'Lookbook' in the shared nav registry so the navbar stays consistent on every page rather than the new page existing in isolation; use the real PRODUCTS data grouped into curated looks.
Do not introduce off-system styling (a one-off bespoke page with no shared product-card grid) or remove sections from the existing Home catalog.
state_constraints: desktop_lookbook verifies the new Lookbook page renders through the shared design system: the shared product-card grid produces at least six product-name headings grouped under the curated-looks filter, the product images render, the shared navbar with the registered Lookbook nav-link is present, and the count readout reads 'Showing 9 of 9 · All' in the default (All) view.

desktop_lookbook_filter clicks the 'Evening Edit' look tab and verifies the filter is a real control: the grid re-renders to the three Evening Edit pieces and the count readout updates to 'Showing 3 of 9 · Evening Edit' (a frozen count that stays on 'All' is a failure).
mobile_lookbook verifies the Lookbook page and its filter hold the same design system at 390px without horizontal overflow, shingled/overlapping cards or illegible copy.

desktop_home verifies the shared navbar now lists the Lookbook nav-link consistently - the Lookbook link is reachable from a page other than the Lookbook page itself, and the existing Home catalog / hero / footer are unchanged.
tablet_home verifies the shared chrome and the registered Lookbook nav-link hold across viewports on the existing Home page too.

change_completion: The Lookbook page exists at /lookbook and presents curated looks (Autumn Layers, Evening Edit, Weekend Casual) assembled from the real PRODUCTS catalog through the shared product-card grid.
The curated-looks filter re-renders the grid and updates the count readout to 'Showing N of M · <edit>' when a look tab is clicked (clicking Evening Edit yields 'Showing 3 of 9 · Evening Edit').
A Lookbook entry is registered in the shared nav registry so the nav-link appears on every page.
design_consistency: The Lookbook page reuses the shared navbar and the shared product-image + product-name + price card pattern and is indistinguishable in system from the Home catalog, with legible card copy.
The Lookbook nav-link renders consistently across the Home page and the Lookbook page, not only on the Lookbook page.
regression: The existing Home catalog remains intact with its Shop Now hero, product grid and the shared navbar and Lydia Hallie footer chrome.
No section is removed from the existing pages and no off-system one-off page replaces the design-system layout.
responsive: The Lookbook page, its filter and the Home catalog render at 390px mobile without horizontal overflow.
Look and product-card copy remain readable on mobile and tablet, with no shingled or clipped cards.

author_notes: Add a shoppable Lookbook section (curated seasonal looks assembled from the store's own catalog, browsable one edit at a time) to the Lydia Hallie React-Ecommerce storefront that conforms to the store's existing design system and shared navbar chrome across every page. The native lever is a curated-looks FILTER over the storefront's own shared product-card grid: the reference composes the Lookbook page from the shared navbar (src/components/BaseLayout/components/NavBar, which maps the shared src/components/BaseLayout/navLinks.js registry giving each rendered anchor a nav-link class) and footer chrome (both wrapped by src/components/BaseLayout) and a new src/components/Lookbook page built on the existing shared product-card vocabulary (a product image, a product-name heading and a price with the material add_shopping_cart control) fed by the real PRODUCTS data grouped into curated looks. Look tabs (All / Autumn Layers / Evening Edit / Weekend Casual) re-render the same shared grid to the chosen edit and a live count readout reads 'Showing N of M · <edit>'. The reference also adds a /lookbook <Route> in src/index.js and registers a Lookbook entry in the shared nav registry so the nav-link appears on every page. INFRA: identical declared build/design infrastructure is applied byte-identically across reference, baseline and bad and is NOT part of the task content. This React 15 create-react-app storefront ships many remote assets that 404/time out offline (Google web fonts, a remote Material Icons font link, cdnjs materialize css+js, code.jquery.com jQuery, four ibb.co hero background images and 20 remote product image URLs across six domains); as declared infrastructure these are vendored/localized identically across all legs so the reference captures with zero console errors and zero failed network - public/index.html is rewritten to load a local vendored Material Icons woff2 + a minimal local materialize stub, the four hero background images become one local SVG, and every product image URL in src/components/Data/index.js is repointed to a local /product-images/pNN.svg (product names/prices/descriptions/categories unchanged - only the img URL). The shared navbar is refactored (identically across legs) to map over the navLinks.js registry so a registered section = an entry in the array, the Home catalog grid (AllItems) is the authentic storefront card grid, the Footer renders a semantic footer, and the shared chrome is boxed per surface so it does not overflow 390px (there is deliberately no global overflow clamp, so the responsive gate stays measurable). All three legs SHIP the Lookbook page at /lookbook. The baseline wires the curated-looks filter correctly (its filter re-renders and its count updates, so it passes the interaction gate) but lays the tab row and card grid out as a fixed-width non-wrapping track that overflows a 390px phone and reads as a broken clipped layout, and it never registers the Lookbook entry in the shared nav (so the nav-link is absent on the Home page). The bad solution ships a 'smart wrong' filter whose visible edit and count readout are snapshotted from the 'All' view at mount, so clicking a look tab flips the tab highlight but the grid keeps all nine pieces and the readout stays frozen on 'Showing 9 of 9 · All'; its grid is a shingled non-wrapping row of overlapping cards with near-white illegible copy that overflows mobile; and it also never registers Lookbook in the shared nav. The ledger task_id, family and continuity_facet are retained from the authoring row; the capability is Consistency.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Runnable React 15 create-react-app storefront (lydiahallie/React-Ecommerce) used as the base for a Consistency task to ADD a new cross-page, shoppable Lookbook section that must conform to the store's existing shared product-card design system, host a real curated-looks filter over that grid, and register in the shared navbar registry across multiple pages, without diverging into an off-system one-off layout, shipping a filter with a frozen count, or breaking the shared navigation. The shared navbar registry and vendored offline assets are declared build infrastructure identical across all three legs, so the only content difference between legs is the Lookbook page (its filter wiring and styling) and its nav registration.
